findings.text: test_every_worker_tool_call_is_answered_by_one_server (and test_a_second_launch_reuses_the_node_server at line 45) start a real reckon.mcp server through subprocess.Popen(start_new_session=True) and never terminate it, so every run of this gate leaves two detached server processes holding a port and a lock inside pytest's tmp_path for the node's lifetime; this node's own measure reads 684 MB resident for that server, and the repository binds against a process that outlives the session that started it.

The recorded resident-memory measure is the same instrument over ten-second windows with two-second sampling (measure-shared-mcp.json holds six samples per arm) while the done_when requires the medians read every ten minutes for one hour per arm; the flat-memory claim the plan rests on is therefore verified over ten seconds, not an hour, and the fragment states the gap but the node's measure remains unmet.

assert answered == WORKERS is tautological: _answered returns len(errors) where errors is the gather of exactly WORKERS coroutines, so the assertion holds whatever the server answers; the real guard is assert errors == [] on line 101, and the misnamed count overstates what the test verifies.

removed = set(servers or {}) - allowed raises TypeError on a list-valued mcpServers because its entries are mappings, so the new list branches at line 697 and line 712 can never be reached; a harness whose mcpServers is a list still raises instead of receiving the shared endpoint the diff was written to deliver.

_write_record keeps a private temporary-and-rename beside reckon/_store.py:636 write_json_atomically, whose docstring states it is the one place a file is published through a sibling temporary; reckon/_worker_fence.py:15 already imports that owner, so the new module forks a capability the repository owns.

node_dir re-implements reckon/node_runtime.py:24 runtime_root_candidate, which exists so every reader resolves one runtime-root order instead of a copy in each, and diverges from it by dropping the TMPDIR fallback, so a node with no /run/user fails at mkdir where the owner would have succeeded.

_pid_alive re-implements reckon/crew/process_liveness.py:11 process_alive and omits its zombie check, so a server whose process has exited but is unreaped is reported live until the port probe happens to fail.
worker_server_config is defined and never called; the harness declarations are composed in _worker_fence.py and _backends.py instead, so the helper is dead surface.

The commit removes about thirty unrelated blank lines across the whole file and drops its trailing line alongside the mcp() option change, folding a lint sweep into a feature commit that the repository requires to be its own commit and that will collide with any peer editing this file.

The two-arm resident-memory measure, the figure that would let a reader see the flat delta at a glance, is delivered as prose only although the node was granted docs/figures/work-scales-to-eighty-across-nodes/wstea-one-mcp-server-per-node-serves-every-worker-that-uses-it and the repository's figure mandate expects a graphic where a graphic carries the result.

item_verdicts.diff: Read commit by commit from bfacff71: 907 insertions across eleven files, the mechanism in reckon/mcp_shared.py, the seams in _backends.py, _worker_fence.py and launch.py, the declaration and validation in flight.py and flight-defaults.yaml, the measure script, the test, and the evidence fragment; project_setup_commands.py also carries unrelated whitespace churn.
item_verdicts.done_when: The done_when asks for 5 then 40 workers, one server process, every tool call answered, and resident medians ten minutes apart over one hour per arm; the gate asserts the first three and the recorded measure answers only the fourth over ten-second windows.
item_verdicts.goal: The node goal is one MCP server per node serving every worker that names it with resident memory flat in worker count; reckon/mcp_shared.py:236 lands it and reckon/_backends.py:3253 wires the launch path to it.
item_verdicts.manifest: The manifest is honest and complete on shape: status complete, five commits cited, the gate command and log path named, the negative control logged, and the one-hour soak admitted as unrun under blockers and rubric.measure.
item_verdicts.write_paths: All eleven changed paths are inside the twelve declared write paths, and the two delivery grants under review-records/ are the only paths written outside the repository.

justifications.durability: tests/test_one_server_per_node_serves_every_worker.py:50 and :103 assert the /proc census equals one pid, which reddens if a second server starts, but no test drives launch_plan with a shared_mcp_servers declaration, and :102 asserts a count the test itself fixes.
justifications.evidence: gate-shared-mcp.log records 5 passed at 80d609fc and measure-shared-mcp.json records 5 workers 683,932 kB against 40 workers 684,972 kB, but the recorded run used --duration 10 --interval 2 (docs/evidence/fragments/work-scales-to-eighty-across-nodes/wstea-one-mcp-server-per-node-serves-every-worker-that-uses-it.html:49) where the done_when requires ten-minute sampling over one hour.
justifications.fit: reckon/mcp_shared.py follows the surrounding module idiom (frozen dataclass, named env constants, module docstring), while tests/test_one_server_per_node_serves_every_worker.py:87 leaves an over-indented call that ruff format would rewrite.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/mcp_shared.py:236 ensure_shared_server starts one node-local server under an exclusive lock and returns its endpoint to every later launcher, and reckon/_backends.py:3253 hands that endpoint to the worker's harness declaration, which is the deliverable §2 states.
justifications.scope_discipline: every changed path in bfacff71..1b72aa39 is inside the twelve declared write paths, but reckon/project_setup_commands.py carries a whole-file blank-line sweep (19 lines of unrelated deletions) folded into the feature commit and reckon/_worker_fence.py:697 adds list-form MCP filtering the goal does not imply.
